blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A harness solves one CP-SAT config (one worker, a fixed seed, no limit) ten times in a loop inside one Python process and passes. The same config fails when each run is its own process. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: In one process hashlib shares one hash salt, so equal plans get one plan digest
options.says: The page says `sorted()` and a SHA-256 digest from `hashlib` do not change with the salt, "because they depend only on the characters"; sha256('P017') printed b61214da6d3c under both seeds.

options.text: In one process the hash salt stays put, so a set keeps its order in the loop
options.says: Right: in one process the set's order never changes; each new process gets a new salt and order.

options.text: In one process the clock is shared, so the runs' wall times stay aligned
options.says: Wall time stays out of the manifest the harness compares, so it cannot fail the check.

options.text: In one process PYTHONHASHSEED is left unset, so hash() turns its salting off
options.says: The page says "unset or `random` means a new salt per process; an integer fixes it; `0` turns the salting off."

origin.section: The Harness Reruns One Snapshot in Fresh Processes

questions.stem: A harness failure reads: run 2 of 3 differs from run 1 at: result.plan, result.plan_digest. The status and objective are not listed. Where should you look first?

options.text: A changed snapshot, which can move the plan while the value holds
options.says: An input change shows under inputs.* in the message; it is not listed.

options.text: Another OR-Tools version, which can pick another plan of equal value
options.says: A version change shows under versions.* in the message; it is not listed.

options.text: A time limit, which can stop each run at another plan of equal value
options.says: A clock limit changes the work counts first; result.stats is not listed.

options.text: A tie, which a seed or build order can break toward another plan
options.says: Right: same value, another plan is a tie; fix the build order or add a tie-break (10.2.1, 10.2.3).

origin.section: It Fails Loudly, and the Failure Points at the Cause

questions.stem: Why do harness.py and the module's tests include a config that is known not to repeat?

options.text: To show the check can fail, since a check that never failed may test nothing
options.says: Right: the design note asks for a known-bad config beside every determinism check.

options.text: To expose a solver bug, so the failing config can be reported upstream
options.says: The page's failing configs are a set-order bug in model code and racing threads, both expected, not solver bugs.

options.text: To count failures, so the report can show how often a config differs
options.says: The page says check stops at the first run that differs, so it counts nothing.

options.text: To give a baseline, so a passing config has a failing digest to compare
options.says: The page says check compares every manifest with the first run of the same config.

origin.section: A Determinism Test Belongs in the Test Suite
